name: AI output evaluator / domain expert (Mercor)
summary: AI-training marketplace that contracts generalists and professionals at hourly rates to judge AI outputs; some roles are open specifically to US and Canada residents.
whatYouDo: You apply to a specific listing. In the US/Canada generalist role you review everyday work files produced by AI (documents, slides, spreadsheets) for quality and accuracy; expert roles (law, STEM, finance, design) ask you to judge or create content in your field.
appeal: Official listing titled 'Generalist Expert (US/Canada)' reported at $50–70/hr
That generalist role reportedly needs no prior AI experience
Several Canada-eligible expert roles at higher rates
Weekly payment via Stripe or Wise (postings and help docs)
watchOuts: Projects can end abruptly; media reported contractors re-offered work at lower rates after a project ended (Mercor disputed this)
A 2026 blog reports a mass offboarding on one project (May 2026)
Some projects require ~15 hrs/week for a few weeks
Mercor's help-centre country list is hard to read; confirm Canada is supported for payment before starting
Independent contractor: no benefits, you handle taxes

credentials: bachelor's degree or equivalent experience (one aggregator copy of the generalist listing); expert roles need domain credentials

training.notes: A blog describes paid onboarding on one project; not confirmed as general policy.

compensation.notes: Generalist Expert (US/Canada) listing, per search summaries of the official page and an aggregator copy (posted 2026-08-16). Currency not stated in snippets. Expert roles in aggregator listings run ~$25–150/hr.

reliability.notes: Reviews call availability 'feast-or-famine'; reported project endings and offboardings in 2026. Anecdotal plus one media report.

applicationSteps: Apply to a listing that names Canada (e.g. Generalist Expert US/Canada)
Complete Mercor's screening for that listing
Sign the contractor agreement and set up Stripe or Wise payouts
fitsIf: You have professional or strong general office skills and want well-paid but short, project-based contracts.
notFitIf: You need ongoing work or dislike sudden project changes.
